artboards.title: Pad Sheet v2 · OUTSIDE, trip out
SPLIT · desk playing, REV + M lit
TAPE SPLICE · the needle, one frame
STACK THE TAKES · 2 picked, one over LIVE
UNDRAWN STATE · SMEAR refused, ghosts on

annotations.text:
PAD SHEET V2 · THE SPEC (Direction A, chosen)
1. The everyday top never changes: header, waveform, provenance, LEVEL / PAN / TUNE, ONE-SHOT / CHOKE / GHOSTS.
2. Every workshop card is a group box with a pixel legend (TREATMENT, SHAPE, MUTATE, OUTSIDE, MAKE), 44 px tap strip, closed by default. Closed, the whole sheet fits one screen.
3. The closed strip reads what the pad carries, from the recipe the code already has: MutateSheet.read, OutsideSheet.read, PadSheet's treatment and shape. "UNTOUCHED" in ink3 when nothing does.
4. One box open at a time. The open box is remembered per kit, not per pad, so A03 ► keeps the same bench open - one job across the whole kit.
5. The pad navigation row is pinned under the scroll area (2 px grayEdge rule above it). EJECT and RE-TRIM scroll with the content.
6. OUTSIDE while a trip is out: the box's summary turns lcd-alt cyan, an LCD strip shows turning reels (the one motion rule: reels spin whenever audio moves), SEND reads the stage dimmed, WET and KEEP ROOM dim, the nav dims. Nothing goes dead.
7. KEEP ROOM lights in lcd-alt only after a ROOM trip; a REAMP dims it. The row always exists, so the box never jumps.
8. Labels: a box strip's summary ellipsizes; a button label ellipsizes; no label may wrap. Budget at 390: about 44 characters in the 8 px pixel face across a full row (6.4 px a glyph beside the chevron), 12 in a three-chip row, 9 in a four-chip row. The shape strip lists only the fields the pad sets.

ROOMS ON THE SHELF (decided)
A third section beside INSTRUMENTS, one row per kept room: Rock Salt name, how it was measured (trip, sureness, the pad, the age), its length on an LCD. Tapping a row does nothing; hold to reveal FORGET → BIN. A forgotten room goes to the bin for 30 days like every other delete - the app's one rule for deletes, kept.

DIRECTION B · WORKSHOP SELECTOR (not chosen)
One segmented row, five benches, one panel.
For: the sheet never grows past one screen.
Against: what the pad carries on the other benches is invisible until you switch; five chips in 366 px is tight - TREATMENT has to become TREAT, and OUTSIDE only just fits.

DIRECTION C · TWO SCREENS (not chosen; two ideas kept)
The sheet keeps only the everyday controls plus an LCD of what the pad carries; WORKSHOP ▸ opens a second screen.
Kept for A: "same bench, next pad" (the open box persists across pads) and the in-flight OUTSIDE strip with turning reels.
Against: two screens deep from the grid; HIT and the waveform repeated on the workshop.

OUTSIDE · THE TRIP, STATE BY STATE (drawn from the code after wave DDD)
The box alone, in order. 1 idle: the status reads what the move will do, in pixel ink; KEEP ROOM dim, UNDO dim. 2 the mic opens before anything plays (LISTENING FOR THE ROOM…): the legend line turns lcd-alt, the reels turn on an LCD strip, SEND reads the stage dimmed, WET dims. 3 the sweep goes out (SENDING… TURN IT UP.). 4 back: the measured line - move, lag, sureness - on an LCD in lcd ink; KEEP ROOM lit in lcd-alt; UNDO live. X refused: nothing came back; the box returns to idle and a toast says why in the verb's own words.
Closed by wave GGG (2026-09-08): OutsideCard now reads the measured line on an LCD strip like every other readout, and KEEP ROOM lights with an amber rim the instant a trip has something to keep - both boards and code agree.

THE LANDING'S HONEST LITTLE MESSAGE BOX (wave FFF, built blind; drawn here to check it)
The capture-blocked dialog's shape, generalised: scrim, raised bevel, the title in LCD type, the lines in a sunken field - trouble first in warn, what landed after - then FINE. Left: a kit file with one skip; the title is the toast's own line. Right: a share the shelf refused - the file's name, then the refuser's words. The refusal is long: the board lets a line wrap to three; the code capped lines at two and clipped this one, so the cap moves to three with these boards. A clean landing never opens the box - the toast stays the one-line voice.

KIT · THE ACTION ROW AND TEXTURE (drawn from the code; DESIGN_GAP's last undrawn pair)
The oldest artboard (`design/TapeOS Oilslick.dc.html`, `isKit`) drew one row of three: EVIL TWINS, TAKES + BIN, KEY, above a big ARM button that has since moved to THE SHELF. The code has grown past that: REMIX BANK B (EVIL TWINS renamed), a second row for SCULPT and STRETCH (TEXTURE didn't exist when that board was drawn), and a full-width SHARE below - five doors and a button where the board drew three. Closed (left), the sheet reads TAKES + BIN, REMIX BANK B, KEY, SCULPT, STRETCH, SHARE, six lines the language never checked together. KEY open (middle): the same panel as PAD SHEET's own KEY door, unchanged. TEXTURE open (right, SCULPT): SOURCE steps the kit's own pads, three mode chips, one knob, GO renders four takes.
What the drawing found: nothing wrong with either panel once open - both fit and read clearly. The six-item closed sheet is dense but each label states its own words in full at 390 (measured, no clipping); grouping it as three text buttons + a three-way row (row 1) then two texture doors (row 2) mirrors PAD SHEET's group-box logic (TREATMENT/SHAPE/MUTATE/OUTSIDE/MAKE) closely enough that a GroupBox pass here is the natural next design step, not an emergency fix - noted below the line, not fixed blind.

GRAIN FIELD (drawn from GrainFieldScreen.kt; never had a board - it arrived from another branch)
Loading: an LCD line while GrainField.analyze runs off-thread. Idle: the scatter (grains near the touch light in accent), the hint line beneath. DUET, no mic: the DUET chip lights, START MIC appears full-width above the hint, which already changes to the headphones warning - the canvas keeps its weight(1f) so the button doesn't crowd it. DUET, armed: the same scatter, an auto-cursor ring at a different radius from the touch ring so the two never read as the same mark (a finger always wins over DUET, per the header chip's own KDoc).

SURFACE (drawn from SurfaceScreen.kt; never had a board - it arrived from another branch)
XY: mode row (XY/XYZ/MORPH + →TAPE + PRINT), PAD ◄ ► + LATCH + BARS, SET A-D dimmed outside MORPH, the touch grid with crosshair and puck, one LCD readout. MORPH: the corner bars and A/B/C/D labels, SET A-D live, and the readout at its longest - latency, X/Y, all four corner weights, TILT, the pad name. No pad: OPEN A KIT over the grid, the readout's pad segment simply absent.
Found and fixed: the readout was one un-wrapped LCD line - at MORPH's longest (latency SHARED, X/Y, all four corners, TILT, a named pad) it ran to roughly double the frame's width and clipped mid-digit. TapeText now allows a second line (`maxLines = 2`); every board here draws that fix, not the clipped original. Below the line: the rare worst case (MORPH + tilt + a shared stream + a long pad name) can still lose the pad name even across two lines - latency already leads the line on purpose, by the code's own comment, so that field survives; a truly lossless layout would need a restructure, not a parameter.

SHARE / BACKUP · THE CHOOSER HAND-OFF (DESIGN_GAP's last undrawn pair, drawn from ShareOut.kt, App.kt's shareKit/backupShelf, LandingNote.kt)
SHARE (top row): the kit is packed off-thread while the sheet reads PACKING… in the status bar's tail cell, every door dimmed to ink3 like any other busy screen. The app then hands the file to Intent.createChooser and steps out of the way - the system's own sheet, not ours, drawn schematically here since SnipSnap owns nothing past this point. Two returns: a clean pick closes the toast 'KIT PACKED AS ONE FILE. PICK WHERE IT GOES.'; no receiving app on the phone (ActivityNotFoundException) never opens a chooser at all and answers in the same one-line toast voice instead - 'NOWHERE TO SEND IT.'
BACKUP (bottom row): the empty shelf never reaches PACKING at all - kits.isEmpty() answers before the busy lock or the chooser, in the toast, BACKUP left visibly dimmed so the gate reads as a rule, not a bug. A backup where preflight skipped a kit answers in the honest little message box instead of the toast, the same shape wave FFF gave the landing side (page four): trouble first in warn, what packed after, FINE.
What the drawing found: no defect - shareKit/backupShelf already route every branch (empty gate, no-receiver, clean, partial) through the app's two existing answer shapes (the one-line toast, the message box) with nothing improvised in between; the only piece with no board before this pass was the chooser hand-off itself, now drawn.

SPLIT (drawn from SplitScreen.kt; EEE9, never had a board - it arrived from another branch)
Not split: a pad chosen, SPLIT lit amber (its own "nothing has happened here yet" cue, the same lit rule KEEP ROOM uses), the desk's three strips visible but disabled at rest (1.00, unity, ink3 knobs) so the shape of what SPLIT does is legible before the maths runs. Working: the spectrogram-and-two-median-filters pass - PAD ◄►, ◄ KIT and the SPLIT button itself all dimmed, the LCD reading WORKING so a slow phone doesn't read as a hang. Desk playing: SINES pushed to 1.35 and reversed (REV lit amber), TRANSIENT at 0.60, AIR pulled to 0.00 and muted (M lit) - three faders, three independent decisions, STOP lit where PLAY was. Printed hot, to TAPE: the desk pushed toward the top of its +6 dB range, the toast carrying the same hot-peak warning PRINT already says aloud rather than quietly turning down - 'SPLIT PRINTED 2.3 S TO TAPE. HOT: PEAK 1.34.'
What the drawing found: no defect - lit, dimmed and enabled states all read from the same ActionButton vocabulary every other screen uses, the fader's own unity tick and amber knob match Fader.kt's drawing exactly, and PRINT's hot-peak warning is said in the same toast voice on both the →TAPE and →PAD paths (the →PAD case is masked by the shared SlotChooserOverlay, out of this page's scope - it already has callers elsewhere and isn't SPLIT's own vocabulary to redraw).

KEYS (drawn from KeysScreen.kt; never had a board - reached from the shelf's INSTRUMENTS row, over InstrumentPlayer/:shell's InstrumentEngine)
CHROMATIC, idle: the LCD header names the instrument and reads ROOT/OCT; a chip row (CHROMATIC/MAJOR/MINOR/MIN PENT, the active one amber-filled) sits over the 4×4 itself - root bottom-left, ascending left-to-right and bottom-to-top, exactly UI_DESIGN's rule. A key with no zone mapped to its note dims to ink3 with a 0.3-alpha border rather than disappearing - TalkBack still finds it and says NOT MAPPED (the same 'unavailable, not absent' rule KeyPad's own comment cites against finding 12). A key held: the pressed cell's fill jumps to a 0.45-alpha ink wash: the label itself never changes colour on press, only the box - matching KeyPad's code exactly, where TapeText's ink/ink3 choice depends only on `enabled`. MAJOR picked: the whole grid relabels to the seven-note scale rather than merely highlighting different chromatic keys - proof the layout picker changes what note a slot *is*, not just how it's decorated; wrong notes are physically impossible in this mode, the point UI_DESIGN.md makes for scale layouts.
What the drawing found: no defect - the header's instrument-name/ROOT-OCT line safely ellipsizes through the same TapeText(maxLines=1) every other LCD line in the app uses (unlike SURFACE's readout, nothing here is data that can't afford to be cut); the disabled-key semantics and touch-Y velocity already carry the accessibility-audit fixes forward correctly.

PAD CAPTURE (drawn from PadCaptureScreen.kt; never had a board - opened by a long-press on an empty KIT pad, over MicSessionService/PadCapture/Classifier)
Not armed: the LCD readout says NOT LISTENING YET, START MIC fills the width, GRAB and HOLD TO REC both present but dimmed to half-opacity labels - their sweep rim stays lit regardless, the same always-on-rim/dim-only-the-label look PrimaryAction and HoldRecordAction share with KitsScreen's own PrimaryAction uses (a pre-existing, deliberate convention, not something this screen invented). Armed, idle: the live level meter and MM:SS elapsed counter read from MicSessionService.level/armedAtElapsedRealtime, GRAB and HOLD TO REC both fully lit. Committing a GRAB: the level meter keeps ticking (armed stays true through a commit - only an EJECT flips it), GRAB reads GRABBING… and both actions dim together, since `committing` is the one guard both share - a HOLD press mid-GRAB-commit is a no-op, not a second write racing the first, per KitWrites's own KDoc.
What the drawing found: no defect - the NOT LISTENING/GRAB hint text's declared maxLines (3 and 2) already covers its longest case at 390 without clipping, unlike SURFACE's readout from an earlier wave; the always-lit rim on a disabled action is shared PrimaryAction/HoldRecordAction behaviour, not a PadCaptureScreen-specific inconsistency.

SNIPS (drawn from SnipsScreen.kt; never had a board - the shelf-level list of every WAV under snips/, reached from KitsScreen's SNIPS ▸ row, never kit-scoped)
Empty shelf: the header still reads a real 0 · 0 B count rather than hiding itself, NO SNIPS YET in the LCD panel below. Playing, USED badge: one row mid-playback (■ STOP replacing ▶ PLAY - the same row's own PLAY is how STOP is spelled, a second tap toggles it off), a second row carrying the USED badge (lit only once the cheap anyPadTaggedWithSourceFile gate finds at least one tagged pad on the shelf - no badge renders at all until that resolves, never a guessed 'not used'). → PAD and → TAPE sit on every row regardless of playback state, always enabled - → PAD is never gated on an already-open kit (the fix this screen's own KDoc calls out by name: SNIPS lives on AppScreen.KITS, where `open` is null by definition, so gating on it would permanently disable the button on this screen's own entry path). Delete confirm: DELETE THIS SNIP? CAN'T UNDO. over a dimmed scrim, the same raisedBevel dialog shape App.kt's CaptureBlockedDialog and KitsScreen's StarterMenu already use.
What the drawing found: no defect - the header's count/size readout is short enough at any realistic snip count/size to never approach 390's budget, and DELETE's fixed bin-red border/glow reads identically here as it does in TakesBinScreen and KitScreen, the one deliberately scheme-invariant color pair in the app.

DELETED KITS (drawn from DeletedKitsScreen.kt; never had a board - the last screen this archaeology pass found. Closes the gap KitsScreen.kt's and Personality.kt's own prior KDocs used to describe accurately: a deleted kit used to have neither a listing nor a restore, unlike TAKES + BIN and ROOMS's own FORGET → BIN)
Empty bin: NOTHING DELETED. in the LCD panel, the plain locked tone SNIPS' own NO SNIPS YET set, not the shelf's usual tape-metaphor quips. List, unarmed: two rows, each name/pad-count/relative-age over a RESTORE chip; days-left reads in warn (amber-orange) at ≤2 days and amber otherwise, the same threshold TAKES + BIN and ROOMS's own binned rows use - a row at 0 days left still shows and still restores, the sweep decides when it's actually gone, not this screen. EMPTY armed: a RESTORE tap disarms it first (the row vanishing shifts everything under the finger, so the very next tap must not read as EMPTY's own second tap), and a real second tap on EMPTY itself swaps the label to TAP AGAIN TO CONFIRM — NO TAKEBACKS, the same three-second self-disarming confirm TakesBinScreen's own EMPTY THE BIN NOW uses, copied verbatim.
What the drawing found: no defect - both EMPTY-button strings are the same ones already proven to fit TakesBinScreen's identical layout, and the fixed bin-red border/glow reads the same scheme-invariant pair SNIPS' own DELETE uses.

TAPE SPLICE + STACK THE TAKES (drawn from TapeSpliceScreen.kt and StackTakesScreen.kt; the September merge's PAD SHEET take-workshops, boards drawn after the code)
SPLICE, pick: HEAD and TAIL chosen from this pad's own recoverable history - LIVE is always a candidate (amber name, never binned until something rewrites it), each row reading its real peak and length (-6.2 DBFS · 0.41 S) or the honest WON'T READ; picked chips wear the accent border. SPLICE, needle: both takes stacked on one LCD each, ONE shared needle over both - the frame where the head hands off to the tail; bright tape is what survives the cut. COMMIT is honest about the seam (SPLICED CLEAN. NO OVERLAP NEEDED. / …A FEW MS OF TAPE OVERLAP WENT IN.), and whatever was live is binned, undoable.
STACK: LIVE pinned on top (KitPad.init demands it be loudest), candidates below with age + facts; picks order softest-first, ▲ moves one softer, three zones is the cap (STACK_MAX_THREE says why: the MPC 2 has four layer slots and LIVE takes one). A pick that peaks over LIVE is SAID beside its row (S2 IS +1.2 DB OVER LIVE…) and left exactly that loud - no auto-gain, per STACK_NO_GAIN. The cost is said before COMMIT: STACK_LOCKS, verbatim, above the button.
What the drawing found: no defect in either - both reuse the row/chip/bin vocabulary exactly; the one judgement call drawn here is SPLICE's needle timestamp riding above the lane (the code draws it in the transport readout - either is honest, the board's placement keeps the eye on the seam).

ARRANGE + THE THREE READ-ONLY ROOMS (drawn from ArrangeScreen.kt, DoublesScreen.kt, XRayScreen.kt, DeletedSnipsScreen.kt)
ARRANGE: GROOVE's variations laid into a song - intro → theme → variation → the turn → reprise → outro, each section's row carrying its bars and its REASON in the arranger's own words (sparse - only the hits at or above the base groove's median velocity). The playing section wears the accent border and a ▶ in its number cell; ■ STOP holds PLAY's slot; REROLL ⚄ rerolls the variation, same structure (ARRANGE_REROLLED). Mixdown runs on first PLAY, cached per plan - MIXING… rides the PLAY button, not a scrim.
DOUBLES: the shelf measured once, grouped at the ring you pick (WITHIN 0.02/0.05/0.10 chips); every cluster header says its own WITHIN so a wider ring reads as what it is; GO ▸ opens that kit on that pad's sheet. The two standing caveats (DOUBLES_RULE, DOUBLES_TRIM_CAVEAT) close the screen - nothing here deletes, moves or merges.
X-RAY: what's inside the file, read-only on purpose - EMPTY slots listed rather than left off, unlabeled fields counted at the foot, never guessed at. No action row by design.
DELETED SNIPS: the fourth bin, nested under SNIPS, same red-pill listing/RESTORE/EMPTY grammar as TAKES + BIN and DELETED KITS - days-left goes warn at ≤2 days.
What the drawing found: no defect in any of the four - all reuse proven vocabulary; ARRANGE's section-reason lines are the one new text pattern, drawn at pxs/ink3 where they can't compete with the mark-type section names.

THREE PROPOSALS (not as-built - each board says which way the code should move, if at all)
1. SURFACE readout, restructured: page seven's own note conceded the worst case (MORPH + tilt + shared stream + long pad name) still drops the pad name even at two wrapped lines. The proposal gives every field its pixels: LAT fixed-left (it already leads the line by the code's own comment), pad name ellipsized in the middle, X/Y fixed-right; corner weights and TILT as micro-bars below - bars read faster than four decimals mid-performance. Same 40px LCD budget.
2. KIT action row, grouped: page five flagged six flat lines as a GroupBox candidate. MAKE (changes what you hear: REMIX BANK B, KEY, TEXTURE) vs KEEP (never touches the sound: TAKES + BIN, SHARE); SCULPT and STRETCH fold into the one TEXTURE door they already share; each row earns a status column. Same GroupBox the pad sheet owns - one open at a time, remembered per kit.
3. SMEAR refused, drawn: the one refusal state page one never drew - SMEAR tapped on a ghosted pad. The segment wears the bin-red border for the toast's 2.6s, the toast names the door to clear, the lit GHOSTS toggle points at it, and the selection never moves off the prior segment. The copy is the code's own exception line, uppercased - worth promoting to a Personality.Copy const beside RETRIM_LAYERED so the voice matches.
